name: Egg, whole, hard-boiled
notes: Reference protein. Heat denatures avidin/ovomucoid → 91–94 % ileal digestibility (Evenepoel 1998).

name: Egg, whole, raw
notes: Raw egg protein: only ~51–65 % ileal digestibility — trypsin inhibitors and native ovalbumin resist proteolysis.

name: Milk, whole 3.25 %
notes: Milk fat carries ~6 % C6–C10 MCFA absorbed via the portal vein.

name: Cheddar cheese
notes: Calcium forms insoluble soaps with long-chain FAs → higher faecal fat than the label assumes.

name: Parmigiano Reggiano (hard, aged)
notes: 24-month proteolysis yields free amino acids & peptides with very high digestibility.

name: Beef liver, pan-fried
notes: Glycogen-rich organ: ~5 g available carbohydrate.

name: Frankfurter / hot dog (beef & pork)
notes: Mechanically separated meat & starch fillers dilute protein quality.

name: Salmon, Atlantic, farmed, baked
notes: EPA/DHA: preferentially incorporated into membranes (structural lipid).

name: Tuna, canned in olive oil, drained
Lentils, boiled
notes: Starch granules encapsulated in intact cotyledon cells (Grundy/Ellis): slow, incomplete amylolysis.

name: Black beans, boiled
notes: Seed-coat anthocyanins & tannins lower protein digestibility.

name: Hummus, commercial
notes: Pureed: cell walls ruptured → matrix advantage of whole chickpeas largely lost.

name: Peanuts, dry-roasted
notes: Whole peanuts: 15–18 % of fat excreted (Traoret 2008).

name: Tempeh
notes: Rhizopus fermentation partially pre-digests protein and phytate.

name: White rice, long-grain, cooked
notes: Polished endosperm: starch fully gelatinised & exposed. Use 'Boiled & cooled' to model retrograded RS3.

name: Black rice (Venere), cooked
notes: Anthocyanin-rich pericarp (cyanidin-3-glucoside).

name: Oats, rolled, dry
notes: β-glucan raises luminal viscosity, slowing lipid & starch absorption.

name: Buckwheat groats, cooked
notes: Rutin & quercetin glycosides.

name: Pasta, durum wheat, cooked al dente
notes: Compact gluten network entraps starch → lower glycaemic response than bread.

name: White bread, commercial sliced
notes: Highly aerated crumb maximises amylase access.

name: Sourdough bread
notes: Lactic acid lowers starch digestibility & phytate.

name: Corn tortilla
notes: Nixtamalisation releases niacin; retrograded starch on cooling.

name: Breakfast cereal, corn flakes
notes: Extrusion/toasting destroys reactive lysine (Maillard) — very low DIAAS.

name: Potato, boiled with skin
notes: Patatin protein is of high quality. Cooling for 24 h roughly triples RS.

name: Broccoli, boiled
notes: Glucosinolate → sulforaphane (myrosinase partially heat-inactivated).

name: Carrots, raw
notes: Carotenoid & lipid release requires cell rupture (cooking, chewing).

name: Onion, raw
notes: Quercetin glycosides & fructans (inulin-type).

name: Artichoke, boiled
notes: Inulin-rich: substantial colonic fermentation.

name: Beetroot, boiled
notes: Dietary nitrate → NO: improves mitochondrial P/O efficiency (Larsen 2011).

name: Mushrooms, white, cooked
notes: Chitin-glucan cell walls are non-digestible.

name: Avocado, Hass
notes: Oleic-rich lipid stored in intact idioblast cells.

name: Olives, green, brined
notes: Hydroxytyrosol & oleuropein aglycone.

name: Apple, raw, with skin
notes: Pectin & peel procyanidins.

name: Banana, green (unripe)
notes: Native type-2 resistant starch (RS2): ~40 % of starch escapes the small intestine.

name: Orange juice, 100 %
notes: Juicing removes the cell-wall matrix: sugars become instantly available.

name: Blueberries, raw
notes: Anthocyanins (delphinidin, malvidin).

name: Kiwifruit, green
notes: Actinidin protease aids protein digestion of co-ingested foods.

name: Almonds, whole, raw
notes: Measured ME 4.6 kcal/g vs 6.1 Atwater (Novotny 2012): lipid locked in intact cotyledon cells.

name: Almonds, whole, dry-roasted
notes: Roasting embrittles cell walls: ME rises vs raw (Gebauer 2016).

name: Almond butter
notes: Grinding ruptures cell walls: ME ≈ Atwater.

name: Walnuts, English
notes: ME 21 % below Atwater (Baer 2016). Ellagitannins → urolithins.

name: Pistachios, dry-roasted
notes: Only ~5 % below Atwater (Baer 2012) — thinner cell walls.

name: Cashews, dry-roasted
notes: ME 16 % below Atwater (Baer 2019).

name: Macadamia nuts
notes: Palmitoleic acid (C16:1n-7) ~ 17 % of fat.

name: Chia seeds, whole
notes: Whole seeds often pass intact; mucilage forms a viscous gel.

name: Flaxseed, ground
notes: ALA-rich; secoisolariciresinol lignans.

name: Coconut meat, fresh
notes: Lauric acid ~47 %, C8+C10 ~13 % of fat.

name: Extra virgin olive oil, high-polyphenol (early harvest)
notes: ≥ 500–800 mg/kg phenolics: oleocanthal, oleacein, hydroxytyrosol → UCP & AMPK signalling (model).

name: Olive oil, refined (light)
notes: Refining strips phenolics: same FA profile, no polyphenol bonus.

name: MCT oil (C8/C10)
notes: Portal absorption, CPT-1-independent mitochondrial entry, rapid ketogenesis.

name: Coconut oil, virgin
notes: Only ~13 % true MCT (C8+C10); lauric acid behaves largely as a long-chain FA.

name: Palm oil
notes: Palmitic-rich: slow postprandial oxidation (DeLany 2000).

name: Butter, salted
notes: ~6 % C6–C10 butyrate-rich milk fat; rest mostly palmitic/stearic.

name: Nutritional yeast, flakes (fortified)
notes: β-1,3/1,6-glucan & mannan cell walls; B-vitamin fortified.

name: Whey protein isolate
notes: Leucine ~11 %: fastest-acting MPS trigger.

name: Micellar casein
notes: Clots in the stomach → slow, sustained aminoacidaemia.

name: Collagen peptides (hydrolysed)
notes: DIAAS = 0 (no tryptophan): cannot support myofibrillar synthesis alone; glycine/proline for connective tissue.

name: Dark chocolate, 70–85 % cocoa
notes: Cocoa butter stearic acid: ~10 % lower absorption; flavanols (epicatechin).

name: Cola soft drink
notes: Liquid sugar: zero matrix, negligible TEF, no satiety compensation.

name: Red wine
notes: Ethanol (no storage pool) is oxidised first; resveratrol & procyanidins.

name: Oat drink, unsweetened
notes: Enzymatically hydrolysed oat starch → maltose: high glycaemic availability.
